title: Stock Returns over the FOMC Cycle
one_line: From 1994 to 2013 the whole US equity premium was earned in even weeks of FOMC cycle time (weeks 0, 2, 4, 6 counted from the scheduled meeting); odd weeks were flat or negative. Staying out in odd weeks doubled the Sharpe ratio (≈0.4 → 0.8).

findings.statement: Week 0 = days −1..3, week 2 = days 9..13, week 4 = 19..23, week 6 = 29..33 (day 0 = scheduled FOMC decision day).
Average 5-day excess returns: week 0 +0.57%, week 2 +0.30%, week 4 +0.42%, week 6 +0.61%; odd weeks −0.17% to 0.
Even-week days earn 10-13.6 bp/day more than odd-week days (1% significance); pattern in all three sub-periods and in international markets.
Strategy 'out of the market in odd weeks': Sharpe ≈ 0.8 vs ≈ 0.4 buy-and-hold, ~3 pp more return, ~1/3 less volatility.

why.pattern: Fed information flow: board meetings and Fed communication cluster in even weeks; stock gains follow news of easier policy.

tradable_edge: New spec fomc_cycle_even_weeks_es: hold ES only in even FOMC weeks (daily close-to-close). Public FOMC calendar (approved for the bundle).

decay_risk.reason: Widely publicized since 2015; later evidence suggests the pattern weakened after 2016.

data_fit: ES 1-min Dec 2013 → Sep 2026, NQ 1-min Jul 2021 → Sep 2026 (2024+ protected in the backtest project).
